approachQuestion.prompt:
Keep Uncontested Readings

A finite acyclic singly linked list has nondecreasing integer values. Remove every node whose value occurs more than once anywhere in the list. Return the remaining original nodes in their original order. Only next links may change; removed nodes need not be cleared. Only head is supplied; 0 <= n <= 200000.

Input: [1,2,2,4,7,7]. Output: [1,4].
Input: [3,3,3]. Output: null. Input: [5]. Output: the original node.

Choose a method that satisfies the full contract with the best worst-case running time, breaking time ties by least auxiliary storage.

options.text: Copy all node references into an array, inspect adjacent values to identify singleton runs, and relink only the singleton references.
options.feedback: This removes whole repeated runs correctly, but stores every reference unnecessarily.

options.text: For each run keep its first node and bypass the rest.
options.feedback: [2,2] would leave one 2, but neither node may remain.

options.text: Whenever current equals current.next, bypass only current.next and continue from current.
options.feedback: On [3,3,3] this keeps a 3 even though the entire value must disappear.

options.text: Use a sentinel and the tail of the kept chain. Scan to the end of each equal-value run; link the run into the kept chain only if it contained exactly one node, otherwise bypass it entirely.
options.feedback: Sorting makes all copies contiguous, so run length decides whether any node of that value may survive.

feedback.reason: Sorting makes all copies contiguous, so run length decides whether any node of that value may survive.
details: Use a sentinel and the tail of the kept chain. Scan to the end of each equal-value run; link the run into the kept chain only if it contained exactly one node, otherwise bypass it entirely.

A repeated run is removed entirely, not reduced to one representative. Sorted order makes each equal run complete locally. The kept tail bypasses the whole run, including duplicates at the original head.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (acm-b15-09-target), regardless of your Q1 choice. Here n. Choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Count each node allocation, link access, identity/value comparison and machine-word operation as constant work. Include all temporary collections and call frames; exclude supplied nodes and the final returned output only. Copying or allocating k records costs k operations. No hash-table, amortized-operation or tail-call assumptions are used.

options.explanation: This pair does not describe the fixed method. Scanning each run advances across each node once; arbitrary sorted inputs still need linear inspection. A sentinel and fixed references/counters suffice. Output reuses original nodes and returns a head reference; there is no recursive stack.
